learningObjective: Identify correct statements about executing an AOTInductor-compiled artifact at runtime.

canonicalClaims.claim: An AOTInductor artifact exposes a C-ABI entry function, bundles the generated Triton/CUDA kernels, and runs without Python and without the Inductor compiler at runtime.
conditions: AOTInductor build succeeded and the target architecture matches the deployment device.
The caller provides device-memory pointers plus shape/stride metadata.
nonImplications: Does not imply arbitrary shapes are supported; only pre-declared dynamic ranges are.
Does not imply a permanently frozen C ABI across all future versions.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor still calls Inductor at first inference.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOT means all lowering has happened before deployment.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor requires the full libtorch at deployment.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOTInductor is designed to avoid full libtorch; it uses a minimal C shim.

misconceptions.claim: Kernels are not bundled; they must be shipped separately.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Generated kernels are packaged with the artifact.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor supports arbitrary dynamic shapes at inference.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only shapes declared as dynamic at build are supported.
